Andrew Ashbaugh, son of Johann Heinrich Eschbach, who came over from Rotterdam in 1738.
He farmed Andrews Burgh, about 121 acres in Mountjoy Township near the Maryland line,
surveyed in 1768, and was probably also a potter like his children and nephews.
He was a founding member of Mark’s German Reformed Church in 1789.
He died on the home farm on 12 March 1814.
His daughter Maria Magdalena married Johann Adam Winterode of Littlestown.
His will, made on 25 March 1813 and signed with his mark, “AEB”, left his wife Mary the use of their room and the
kitchen, a cow of her choice and a third of the farm’s yearly produce, and charged his executors to see that she was
“treated with respect and humanity”. His son Alexander was to have the first offer to rent the farm;
after Mary’s death the land was to be sold and shared equally among all the children.
He named as executors his son Thomas and “my Son in Law Adam Winterode”.
The will was proved at Gettysburg on 10 September 1814.
Wife of Andreas Eschbach (Andrew Ashbaugh) of Mountjoy Township, Adams County, Pennsylvania,
recorded as Maria Artemesia and in several other spellings: Dessime, Odessima, Tessime.
Her maiden name is unknown. She outlived her husband and died in Adams County in 1819.
